sources.molar_mass: 2 × H 1.0080 g/mol: CIAAW abridged standard atomic weights 2024, https://www.ciaaw.org/abridged-atomic-weights.htm
sources.molar_heat_capacity: C_v at 298.15 K = C_p − R = 28.836 − 8.314 J/(mol·K). C_p of H2(g) at 298.15 K: NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, table H-050, https://janaf.nist.gov/tables/H-050.html. R: CODATA 2018, 8.314462618 J/(mol·K)
sources.phase: NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69), Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems, hydrogen (normal): boiling_point is the saturation temperature at 101.325 kPa, and latent_heat_vaporization the vapour minus liquid enthalpy there, 0.904547 kJ/mol, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Load&ID=C1333740&Type=SatT&Digits=6&PLow=0.101325&PHigh=0.101325&PInc=0&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm. melting_point is the triple-point temperature, the lowest saturation temperature in the same data, which the melting point at 101.325 kPa differs from by under 0.1 K. No latent_heat_fusion: no reference value was checked
